(def ^boolean =
  "Equality. Returns true if x equals y, false if not. Compares
  numbers and collections in a type-independent manner.  Clojure's immutable data
  structures define -equiv (and thus =) as a value, not an identity,
  comparison."
  (fn ([x] true)
  ([x y]
    (if (nil? x)
      (nil? y)
      (if (suss.bootstrap/number? x)
        (if (suss.bootstrap/number? y)
          (suss.bootstrap/equiv x y)
          (if (satisfies? ICollection y) (-equiv y x) false))
        (if (instance? Keyword x)
          (identical? x y)
          (or (suss.bootstrap/equiv x y)
            ^boolean (-equiv x y))))))
  ([x y & more]
     (if (= x y)
       (if (next more)
         (recur y (first more) (next more))
         (= y (first more)))
       false))))

The identity fast path is qualified to the compiler-owned strict primitive so rebinding the public identical? var cannot alter equality or the pinned comparator predicate-rebinding observations. Numbers are equal only within a category, as Clojure's Util.equiv: (= 1 1.0) is false (#336). As in Util.equiv, a number is compared with another number directly and asks only a collection on the right, never dispatching -equiv on the number. A keyword on the left answers by identity, as Clojure's interned Keyword.equals does, without -equiv dispatch (#361).
